Patient: I was skiing in Vermont, and I caught my ski when I was coming off the lift, which made me fall. My knee popped, and it's hurt ever since. I don't think I've ever had a previous knee injury or surgery.
Doctor: Did you experience any immediate swelling or bruising after the injury, and if so, when did it occur?
Patient: I didn't notice any immediate swelling or bruising right after the fall, but it's been pretty swollen and painful ever since. I haven't really looked at it closely for bruising, to be honest.
Doctor: Have you experienced any locking, clicking, or giving way of the knee since the injury?
Patient: Yes, the knee feels like it's going to buckle when I try to put weight on it, and it's been really unstable. I haven't noticed any locking or clicking, just a constant pain on the outside and the feeling that it won't hold me up.
Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging studies, such as an X-ray or MRI, for this knee injury?

reference_so.subjective:
Basic information: Michelle, 34, presented with knee injury following a skiing incident last weekend. Chief complaint: pain, instability, and inability to bear weight on the affected knee.

History of present illness: Michelle sustained a knee injury during a skiing incident in Vermont when she caught her ski while coming off the lift, leading to a fall. She reported a popping sound at the time of injury, followed by pain, instability, and inability to bear weight on the affected knee. She was assisted by the ski patrol and has not experienced any prior knee injury or surgery. She mentioned that there was no immediate swelling or bruising right after the fall, but it has been swollen and painful ever since. She hasn't closely examined it for bruising. The knee feels like it's going to buckle when she tries to put weight on it, and it's been really unstable. She hasn't noticed any locking or clicking, just a constant pain on the outside and the feeling that it won't hold her up. The pain is on the outside of her knee, near the lateral side, and it doesn't really radiate anywhere else. It's pretty focused right there, and it hurts a lot when she tries to straighten her leg all the way.

Past history: No prior knee injuries or surgeries. No relevant allergies or personal/family history provided.
reference_so.objective:
Physical examination: Physical examination revealed swelling and tenderness over the medial joint line. Range of motion was limited due to pain, and there was a positive Lachman test indicating possible anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) involvement. No immediate bruising was noted, but there was mild effusion. No numbness, tingling, or changes in the color or temperature of the leg or foot. Normal toe movement.

Investigations: Imaging studies: X-ray performed, no bone issues detected. MRI ordered to evaluate for ligament damage, including possible ACL tear.
